name: chem-r3
context:
A dice puzzle game is adding a chemistry layer. This is a re-audit: an earlier verdict of APPROVE was obtained by extracting text from the model's reasoning trace rather than from an emitted answer, which was judged invalid evidence. The approval is therefore withdrawn and the design is being submitted again for a committed verdict.

EXISTING GAME: a 6x6 board; each cell shows a die face 1-6 and an integer charge 0-3. Each cell also has a HIDDEN link to one neighbour; charge travels along those links and the player infers the hidden structure by watching it.

THE DESIGN AS REVISED:
- Valence is DERIVED from group number, never hand-assigned: groups 1-2 valence = group; groups 14-17 valence = 18 - group. So H=1, O=2, N=3, C=4.
- Faces 1-4 carry valence 1-4. Faces 5 and 6 are NOBLE GASES: valence 0, inert, unbondable, acting as obstacles. This was forced by measurement: under uniform face weights 34% of tiles would otherwise be valence 5-6, and those appear in none of the 11 playable library molecules, because the hypervalent species needing them (PCl5, SF6) are 6-7 atoms and too large for the region sizes that are playable.
- The player selects a connected REGION of cells (not a path: a path gives interior atoms degree 2 and endpoints degree 1, so carbon could never appear in one; methane is a plus-shape). The game then solves for an assignment of bond orders 1-3 to adjacent pairs such that every selected atom's total bond order exactly equals its valence. This is a perfect b-matching and it is what deriving a Lewis structure is.
- A satisfiable region must ALSO match a real molecule from a curated library, or it does not score. This is the scarcity mechanism.
- Score is ENTHALPY CHANGE: bonds broken minus bonds formed. Energy released, not energy collected.
- The hidden link is a reaction pathway that carries charge. It is NOT molecular geometry, and no VSEPR claim is made anywhere in code, copy or comment. An oracle will enforce that textually.
- A dangling unsatisfied valence at end of turn busts the turn, as in Farkle.

MEASURED, 60 boards, uniform face weights, all 1613 connected regions of size 2-5: single bonds only leaves 50/60 boards with at least one satisfiable molecule (mean 4.3); allowing doubles gives 60/60 (mean 15.9); allowing triples gives 60/60 (mean 40.9). Requiring the region to also BE a real molecule cuts 40.9 to 10.3 per board, with 59/60 boards retaining at least one.

NOT in scope and not to be assumed: electronegativity, polarity, ionic bonding, catalysts, pH, explosives, isotopes.

questions.text: Does deriving valence from group number survive a chemist's reading, or is the die-face-to-valence mapping still a superficial coincidence?
Is 10.3 real molecules per board the right scarcity for a puzzle, and if not, in which direction is it wrong?
Does scoring by enthalpy change actually teach chemical stability, or is it a real number used decoratively?
Name the most specific piece of real chemistry this design would still teach WRONGLY, given that the VSEPR/geometry claim has been removed.
Is making faces 5 and 6 noble gases an honest fix, or a patch that conceals a mapping that does not fit a six-sided die?
